question:
A silicon diode is used in a biasing circuit with a $3.3\,\text{V}$ supply and a series resistor $R$ to control forward current. The diode forward drop is not constant; due to device variation and temperature it can lie between $0.65\,\text{V}$ and $0.75\,\text{V}$ in the intended operating range.

(a) Design $R$ so that the diode forward current never exceeds $5\,\text{mA}$ for any allowed diode drop in the range. Show the inequality you use and compute a suitable standard-value resistor.

(b) Using the diode exponential law idea, the student argues: “A small increase of $0.05\,\text{V}$ in forward bias can multiply the current by a large factor, so a resistor is essential for stable biasing.” Quantitatively support this statement by estimating the factor</br>

 $\frac{I_2}{I_1}=\exp\left(\frac{\Delta V}{V_T}\right)$ </br>

for $\Delta V=0.05\,\text{V}$ at $300\,\text{K}$, taking $V_T\approx 0.026\,\text{V}$ (assume ideality factor $\eta=1$ for estimation).

(c) Evaluate the following claim and justify: “If we remove $R$ and connect the diode directly across $3.3\,\text{V}$, the diode current will still remain near $5\,\text{mA}$ because the diode drop self-adjusts.”

(d) Draw the circuit diagram of the series-biased diode and superimpose a qualitative load line on a diode $I$–$V$ curve to show how $R$ controls the operating point.

(e) Suggest one modification to make the operating point less sensitive to diode parameter variation and briefly justify.

options.A: Choose $R\ge \dfrac{3.3-0.65}{5\times 10^{-3}}\approx 530\,\Omega$ (e.g., $560\,\Omega$ standard); current ratio for $0.05\,\text{V}$ is $\exp(0.05/0.026)\approx 6.84$ showing strong sensitivity; direct connection is unsafe because current can become very large; load line explains stabilization; adding a larger $R$ (or using a current-limiting design) reduces sensitivity.
options.B: Choose $R\ge \dfrac{3.3-0.75}{5\times 10^{-3}}\approx 510\,\Omega$; current ratio is about $1.2$ so resistor is not essential; direct connection is safe because diode clamps voltage; load line is unnecessary.
options.C: Choose $R=0\,\Omega$ because the diode will self-limit at $0.7\,\text{V}$; current ratio is $\exp(0.05\times 0.026)\approx 1.001$; direct connection is always safe.
options.D: Any $R$ works because diode current is fixed by doping; current ratio is independent of temperature; removing $R$ does not change the operating point.
